_comment: Native intensity-trace tool, drawn by emtk.view_form over gui/app.py's _Form (the model's fields, the app's actions). Two panels shown as the Qt widget's two tabs; the detector list is the custom section `detectors` (one tick per detector of the setup, else per routing channel). The plots and the result views are dock windows drawn by gui/app.py.

sections.description: Open a TTTR file, choose the detector setup, help and the guided tour.

buttons.label: Load TTTR
buttons.description: Open a TTTR file (PTU, HT3, SPC, HDF5, ...) and bin it into an intensity trace; a dropped file does the same.

buttons.label: Example
buttons.description: Load a simulated molecule switching between two FRET states (dwell 20 / 80 ms, two detectors): data whose answer is known, for trying the tool.

buttons.label: Help
buttons.description: What the trace, the histograms and the hidden Markov model show, and what Compute HMM writes.

buttons.label: Guide
buttons.description: A step-by-step walk through the tool, pointing at each control.

sections.label: File
sections.description: The TTTR file being shown (load another with Load TTTR or drop one on the window).

sections.label: Setup
sections.description: The detector setup: which routing channels (and micro-time ranges) make each detector. 'Routing channels' bins every routing channel on its own.

buttons.label: Edit setups
buttons.description: Open the detector setup editor (setups, PIE windows, detectors, LUT handling, optical setup): the Qt tool's Setup dialog. A change re-bins the file.

sections.label: ms
sections.description: Width of one bin of the trace, in milliseconds; the file is binned again when it changes.

buttons.label: Save Traces
buttons.description: Write the traces (and the HMM state, once computed) to a CSV file.

sections.title: Detector Selection
sections.description: The detectors (or routing channels) that are binned; each ticked one is its own trace.

sections.label: Bins
sections.description: Number of bins of the count histograms beside the traces.

sections.label: Min Counts
sections.description: Lowest count per bin included in the histograms.

sections.label: Max Counts
sections.description: Highest count per bin included in the histograms.

buttons.label: Compute HMM
buttons.description: Fit a hidden Markov model of the chosen number of states to the trace, then write burst IDs, traces and histograms beside the file (<file>_HMM#<n>_<ms>ms).

sections.label: HMM Components
sections.description: Number of hidden states of the model.

buttons.label: BIC Elbow
buttons.description: Fit models of 1 to 15 states and plot their BIC: the elbow is the number of states the data supports.

buttons.label: HMM Matrix
buttons.description: The transition probabilities between the states.

buttons.label: Dwell Times
buttons.description: How long each state lasts: histograms with single-exponential fits.

buttons.label: FRET Distributions
buttons.description: FRET efficiency (first detector over the sum) of the bins in each state; needs two detectors.

sections.description: Show the results of the model.

sections.label: Min Bin
sections.description: Shortest dwell time in the histograms.

sections.label: Max Bin
sections.description: Longest dwell time in the histograms.

sections.label: Number of Bins
sections.description: Number of bins of each dwell-time histogram.

sections.label: Normalize Histogram
sections.description: Show each histogram as fractions of its dwells.

buttons.label: Save Histograms and Fits
buttons.description: Write every state's histogram and its fit (A, tau) to a CSV file.
